answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a public registry, like a marble slab listing every verified identity, before it may transact. A sparrow-sized stake is cheap for one real agent but ruinous at the scale of a thousand fakes, and a dawn audit that randomly re-checks a sample of identities each epoch slashes the stakes of fakes, so an attacker must keep paying to stay in the game while honest agents earn their stake back through useful work.
